title: Pat Karney: Tributes to Manchester political giant

evidence_packet.title: Pat Karney: Tributes to Manchester political giant
evidence_packet.lead: Pat Karney, who had been receiving treatment for cancer, had sat on Manchester City Council since 1979
evidence_packet.summary: Pat Karney, who had been receiving treatment for cancer, had sat on Manchester City Council since 1979
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Pat Karney: Tributes to Manchester political giant - BBC News Image source, Manchester City Council Image caption, Pat Karney has died aged 78 By Marc Waddington North West Published 1 hour ago Tributes have been paid to "a giant" of Manchester's political scene on his death at the age of 78. Pat Karney had represented Harpurhey for Labour since 1979 and had been well-known as the authority's city centre spokesman. He had been suffering from cancer and had been having treatment at The Christie hospital. Manchester City Council leader Garry Bridges said he was "Manchester through and through and he never lost his determination to champion the city or his astute political judgement". Karney was born in Dublin and moved to Manchester as a boy. Proud of his Irish roots, he played a prominent role in the city's Irish Festival. He helped drive the regeneration of Manchester city centre following the 1996 IRA bombing and masterminded the first Manchester Day celebrations in 2010. A long-standing champion of gay rights, he also played a leading role in Manchester City Council's opposition to Section 28, which prohibited local authorities and state-funded schools from "promoting homosexuality". 'Great sense of fun' Bridges said: "Pat was a giant of Manchester politics and one of the city's most recognisable public figures for nearly 50 years. "He never lost his connection to where he came from. He was proud to be from Collyhurst and to represent the people of Harpurhey and Collyhurst." He said that although Karney was "deeply serious about his politics and his values", he also had "a great sense of fun" and was not afraid to use "a gimmick or two" to get his message across. Patsy McKie's youngest son Dorrie, 20, was shot dead in the Hulme area of Manchester in 1999. Just days later, she co-founded Mothers Against Violence (MAVUK) and dedicated the rest of her life to travelling across the world to raise awareness of her anti-crime campaign. A colourful mural has been painted at the MAVUK Hulme Centre following her death in January 2025 at the age of 77. "She was a very bright person, even through some of the most difficult periods of her life," said her son, Ian Swanston. "She wanted to bring a sense of colour to the world. "A creative artwork representing Patsy would have to be colourful, because that's definitely what she wants." Image caption, Patsy McKie began campaigning against violent crime after her son's death Dorrie has been about to start a sports and leisure course at college when he was shot dead amid spiralling gang violence in Manchester. Patsy believed deeply in the strength of community and in the possibility of healing, even during the most difficult of times. "She always said that if young people are doing something positive, they won't have time to do the things that are negative in our community," said Ian. "So she really wanted to be able to create spaces that allowed young people to excel." evidence_packet.summary: Michelle Pearson called 999 hours before a fatal arson attack killed her four children in 2017
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A police officer has admitted "nothing" was done to keep a mother and her four children safe in the hours before they were murdered in an arson attack At an inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court, PC Mike Grundy said he did not think there was a "risk of fire" at the home of Michelle Pearson and her four children in Walkden, Salford - despite Zak Bolland having made threats to "petrol bomb" the property Four of Michelle's children were murdered in the arson attack on 11 December 2017; Michelle, 37, died in August 2019, after being badly burned Bolland and David Worrall were jailed for life in 2018 for the murder of the four children, and convicted in 2021 of Michelle's murder Bolland was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 40 years, and Worrall was sentenced to life with a minimum of 37 years in jail The court previously heard Grundy and PC Gemma Quinn went to the scene in Walkden around 01:25 GMT on 11 December 2017, after Michelle called 999 because Bolland and three others were outside her house

title: What Manchester's 'super-profit' deal with City owners has paid out so far

evidence_packet.title: What Manchester's 'super-profit' deal with City owners has paid out so far
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester City Council has made almost £3m from the "super-profits" of Man City-linked developments
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester City Council has made almost £3m from the "super-profits" of Man City-linked developments
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Council has made just under £3m from a deal to share in the so-called "super-profits" from developments built on its land by Manchester City's owners A deal struck in 2014 meant the council would receive payments if the profits made by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) on schemes in Ancoats and New Islington exceeded a certain level But Prof Adam Leaver, co-author of a 2022 report by the University of Sheffield into the council's relationship with ADUG, said commercial secrecy around the arrangements meant it was hard to know if the council got the best value it could The council said it expected another payment soon, and that the regeneration had been worth £1.25bn to the city In 2008, Manchester City was bought for £200m by ADUG, owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan - a senior member of the Abu Dhabi ruling family, who is a current vice president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) In the next decade, the club went on to win the first three of eight Premier League titles, and ADUG and Manchester City Council became partners in a company called Manchester Life

title: Public inquiry over Manchester synagogue attack deaths

evidence_packet.title: Public inquiry over Manchester synagogue attack deaths
evidence_packet.lead: The Home Secretary confirms a public inquiry will examine Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby's deaths
evidence_packet.summary: The Home Secretary confirms a public inquiry will examine Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby's deaths
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Public inquiry over Manchester synagogue attack deaths - BBC News Image source, Family handouts Image caption, Adrian Daulby, left, and Melvin Cravitz, right, were killed in the attack on the synagogue in Manchester By Daniel Wittenberg North West Published 12 October 2026 Updated 13 October 2026 A public inquiry will examine the deaths of two men killed during an attack at a synagogue in Manchester last year. Melvin Cravitz, 66, died from multiple stab wounds and fellow worshipper Adrian Daulby, 53, was killed by a bullet fired by armed police as he blocked the synagogue doors when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, tried to get in the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue on 2 October 2025. Announcing the inquiry, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: "What happened that day must be fully understood." Syrian-born UK citizen Al-Shamie was shot dead by police while carrying out the attack. Police had already seized Al-Shamie's mobile phone containing details of his "extremist mindset", but did not analyse the contents until after he had attacked the synagogue. The attack took place on Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the year for Jews. Mahmood said: "In recent days, we marked the first anniversary of the terror attack at the Heaton Park synagogue. "On that awful day in October of last year, as our Jewish community celebrated Yom Kippur, two brave men – Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby – lost their lives, and three others were seriously injured. "What happened that day must be fully understood. "So, as requested by the coroner, I can today announce a public inquiry into the deaths of Mr Cravitz and Mr Daulby. "This will ensure that all evidence can be heard, including any sensitive national security material that could not otherwise be fully heard in the coroner's court." Image sourc

title: Our memorial garden helps us grieve - a cemetery felt too far away

evidence_packet.title: Our memorial garden helps us grieve - a cemetery felt too far away
evidence_packet.lead: Emma Moore shares how creating a special place at home has helped her family
evidence_packet.summary: Emma Moore shares how creating a special place at home has helped her family
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Our memorial garden helps us grieve - a cemetery felt too far away - BBC News Image source, Emma Moore Image caption, Emma Moore says the garden has given her family, including elder daughter Penelope, a focus following the death of baby Mabel By George Sandeman Published 14 October 2026, 01:06 BST Updated 19 minutes ago When Emma Moore's daughter Mabel died, visiting her in a cemetery felt too far away. "I don't like going to them and I feel like [visits] fizzle out," she says. "At first, you'll go regularly and then it'll start being once a year." Mabel was born prematurely at 27 weeks in April, her lungs had not fully developed and she lived for just two days. Emma keeps Mabel's ashes next to a photograph of her tiny feet but she wanted a special place to feel close to her. "So we created something in the garden... [to] always be reminded of her every day," she tells Morning Live . The stillness of green spaces "can help us connect with memories" of loved ones, says Andy Langford, clinical director at Cruse Bereavement Support. And there are ways to create a special place of calm to remember anyone you've lost - even if you don't have a garden or know much about plants. Image source, Emma Moore Image caption, Emma, with her partner Louis and daughter Penelope, says the garden reminds them of Mabel each day "I'd never done anything like this before, so I had no clue about where to start," says Emma, 35, who lives near Bolton with her partner Louis and daughter Penelope. She chose to dedicate a part of the garden with a willow tree to Mabel. "I've enjoyed doing the gardening and planting. It was nice to focus on something." Of all the flowers the family have planted in Mabel's garden, Emma's favourite are the lilies. Morning Live - Memorial Gardens Families speak about

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Council has made just under £3m from a deal to share in the so-called "super-profits" from developments built on its land by Manchester City's owners A deal struck in 2014 meant the council would receive payments if the profits made by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) on schemes in Ancoats and New Islington exceeded a certain level But Prof Adam Leaver, co-author of a 2022 report by the University of Sheffield into the council's relationship with ADUG, said commercial secrecy around the arrangements meant it was hard to know if the council got the best value it could The council said it expected another payment soon, and that the regeneration had been worth £1.25bn to the city In 2008, Manchester City was bought for £200m by ADUG, owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan - a senior member of the Abu Dhabi ruling family, who is a current vice president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) In the next decade, the club went on to win the first three of eight Premier League titles, and ADUG and Manchester City Council became partners in a company called Manchester Life

It comes as commuters brace themselves for two more weeks of travel chaos. Three major lines will be shut from Monday (October 19) until next month The closures are the second phase of works to ‘future proof’ the tracks around Cornbrook, Deansgate-Castlefield and Trafford Bar. Around four kilometres of rail which is coming to the end of its 30-year lifespan will be replaced, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has said The works, expected to finish by Sunday, November 1, will mean that no trams will run on the Altrincham , Eccles and Trafford Centre lines. Further disruptions will impact the East Didsbury and Manchester Airport lines, which will stop at Firswood, while the Rochdale line will st The network has been hit by a series of major works over the course of 2026, including a three-week closure on the same stretch during the summer But passengers will get a reprieve in 2027, with just one major round of work scheduled for the year, Metrolink network director Ian Davies said. That will again see the stations around Cornbrook close and is expected to take place over the Easter school holidays

From just a few hundred yards away the 1,000ft high TV mast is invisible in the mist Underfoot the ground is so boggy it wobbles like blancmange. Stood halfway up Winter Hill on a sodden Monday morning, it's hard to imagine this was the scene of one of the UK's worst wild fires. But back in the summer of 2018 that's exactly what it was Then conditions on the moor on the border of Bolton and Blackburn were very different. The UK was in the midst of a prolonged heatwave leaving the grass and peat parched So, when a fire was started deliberately near the mast authorities were on high alert. To make matters worse the following day a second blaze broke out on another part of the moor And when on the third day the wind changed direction and the fires joined up, it was a recipe for disaster. It was unforgivable' Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 18:43, 13 Oct 2026 View Image Sanela Osmanovic, pictured A cruel thief pretended to befriend an 82-year-old then shoved her to the ground in a 'unforgivable' mugging. Sanela Osmanovic watched the pensioner withdraw £300 from a cash point in Moss Side before following her to a bus stop on Moss Lane East, Manchester Crown Court heard There the 44-year-old struck up conversation by asking the victim her age. When she replied saying she was born 'in 1942 during the Second World War' Osmanovic said: "I can't believe it. You look 65 to 70." The victim then hugged Osmanovic and told her she was kind, only for the thief to push her to the floor and steal her handbag containing the money and an iPhone. She was later seen on CCTV carrying the bag and arrested The victim was taken to hospital, where she was found to have a fractured spine, although medics were unable to ascertain if the injury had been sustained in the attack on April 17 last year. The Jewish Representative Council of Greater Manchester and Region, in a statement on Tuesday, said it had 'concerns' over 'the potential consequences of inflammatory rhetoric f The Heaton Park shows - on July 3 and 4 next year - were announced last month. Fontaines D.C. also announced shows in Cardiff, Newcastle, Glasgow and London as part of a UK headline tour, and are set to be supported by Little Simz and Viagra Boys The band has expressed its support for Palestine at previous shows. Around four kilometres of rail which is coming to the end of its 30-year lifespan will be replaced, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has said The works, expected to finish by Sunday, November 1, will mean that no trams will run on the Altrincham , Eccles and Trafford Centre lines. Further disruptions will impact the East Didsbury and Manchester Airport lines, which will stop at Firswood, while the Rochdale line will st The network has been hit by a series of major works over the course of 2026, including a three-week closure on the same stretch during the summer But passengers will get a reprieve in 2027, with just one major round of work scheduled for the year, Metrolink network director Ian Davies said. That will again see the stations around Cornbrook close and is expected to take place over the Easter school holidays

evidence_packet.lead: Manchester Airport Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule' He has hit out at the autopay system at Manchester Airport, but they have defended the fine Add to preferred s A man has slammed Manchester
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Airport Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule' He has hit out at the autopay system at Manchester Airport, but they have defended the fine Add to preferred s A man has slammed Manchester
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule' He has hit out at the autopay system at Manchester Airport, but they have defended the fine Add to preferred s A man has slammed Manchester Airport after his wife was issued a £100 fine - despite their car being registered for automatic payments at drop-off zones. Michael Joseph said the fine 'undermines the autopay system' after they were charged for dropping their son off at the airport The 52-year-old said his partner took their son to the Terminal 2 pick-up zone on September 23. The family, from Salford , previously set up autopay after having 'a bad experience with parking at the airport' The system allows people to register their vehicle online with a payment card and be automatically charged for pick-ups or drop-offs at the airport If drivers don't have autopay set up, they have to visit Manchester Airport's website - or call up - to pay charges by midnight the day after visits. Missing the payment deadline results in a £100 Parking Charge Notice View 4 Images They received the fine despite having an AutoPay account (Image: Manchester Evening News)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Winter Hill fires How '4,000 holes in Blackburn, Lancashire' are protecting us against wildfires Eight years on from the devastating fires of 2018 Winter Hill is still recovering, but a huge new scheme to 'rewet' the moor hopes to prevent future disas Add to preferred sources Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 05:48, 14 Oct 2026 The rain is coming down sideways. From just a few hundred yards away the 1,000ft high TV mast is invisible in the mist Underfoot the ground is so boggy it wobbles like blancmange. Stood halfway up Winter Hill on a sodden Monday morning, it's hard to imagine this was the scene of one of the UK's worst wild fires. But back in the summer of 2018 that's exactly what it was Then conditions on the moor on the border of Bolton and Blackburn were very different. The UK was in the midst of a prolonged heatwave leaving the grass and peat parched So, when a fire was started deliberately near the mast authorities were on high alert. To make matters worse the following day a second blaze broke out on another part of the moor And when on the third day the wind changed direction and the fires joined up, it was a recipe for disaster. At the height of the blaze 150 firefighters were battling the flames as helicopters dropped hundreds of thousands of litres of water on the moors

title: Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78

evidence_packet.title: Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78
evidence_packet.lead: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources New
evidence_packet.summary: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources New
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources News Dianne Bourne Lifestyle Editor 00:20, 14 Oct 2026 Updated 06:27, 14 Oct 2026 It's about as fitting as it gets that the final social media post from Councillor Pat Karney was one celebrating Manchester and Christmas , two of his greatest passions. No Relentlessly enthusiastic, and fiercely proud of his home city, he was always trying to make things better for the communities he served so tirelessly for the past 50 years As Manchester's self-appointed Christmas spokesperson, he was the man the council relied on to pull on an elf hat, the Christmas jumper, and ensure everyone was ready to celebrate - even if it was the start of November. He ensured the markets every year would get bigger and bette He was also instrumental in bringing the now annual Christmas Parade to life, after the success of the Manchester Day parade, his brainchild, was started in 2010. These events, which bring joy to thousands of people each year, are a special part of Pat's legacy But then Pat sure did love a parade - a regular at Manchester Pride, The St Patrick's Day Parade and Manchester Day. When his home patch of Harpurhey started its own parade in 2025, he hailed walking in it as "the proudest moment of my life."

The victim then hugged Osmanovic and told her she was kind, only for the thief to push her to the floor and steal her handbag containing the money and an iPhone. title: Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled

evidence_packet.title: Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled

evidence_packet.summary: Heaton Park Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled Statements have been issued Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 18:20, 13 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Fontaines D.C
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Heaton Park Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled Statements have been issued Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 18:20, 13 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Fontaines D.C. (Image: Kenny Brown) A Jewish council has called for gigs at Heaton Park by Irish rock band Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled. The Jewish Representative Council of Greater Manchester and Region, in a statement on Tuesday, said it had 'concerns' over 'the potential consequences of inflammatory rhetoric f The Heaton Park shows - on July 3 and 4 next year - were announced last month. Fontaines D.C. also announced shows in Cardiff, Newcastle, Glasgow and London as part of a UK headline tour, and are set to be supported by Little Simz and Viagra Boys The band has expressed its support for Palestine at previous shows. Pictures show the phrases 'free Palestine' and 'Israel is committing genocide' appearing on screens during a gig by the band in London last year The JRC said it had 'registered [its] profound concerns' with Manchester council over the Heaton Park shows. The statement said it expected 'robust and adequate safeguards' to be in place 'to protect the Jewish community' In response, the council said addressing any concerns from the Jewish community would be 'front and centre in preparations for these events'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Gunman shot at woman before barricading himself in stranger's house in four-hour stand-off with armed police Adam Wass has been jailed Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 18:05, 13 Oct 2026 View 4 Images Adam Wass, 3 A gunman who shot at a woman before a four-hour standoff with armed police has been jailed. 'Dangerous' Adam Wass barricaded himself in a terrified stranger's house after twice pulling the trigger of a firearm in Salford He has now been locked up for six years. The 36-year-old, Greater Manchester Police said, put two innocent people through 'terrifying ordeals' Wass attempted to shoot at a woman on St Joseph's Drive, Ordsall, on February 1 this year. The weapon misfired and no bullet emerged from the chamber Wass pulled the trigger again as the woman ran and took cover behind a car. That time, a bullet was fired. GMP said Wass then went into a nearby home and threatened a man inside, who fled unhurt Armed officers were scrambled at around 8.15pm. Wass, who still had the gun, barricaded himself inside and refused to give himself up

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton councillor switches allegiance just 10 weeks after being elected New Green councillor Yusuf Davda said his decision had not been 'taken lightly or out of frustration with others' Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local dem A Bolton councillor who was elected 10 weeks ago has switched allegiance and joined the Green Party. Coun Yusuf Davda recently topped the poll in a by-election for Rumworth ward on July 30 as an Independent He gained 1.458 votes with Labour in second on 1,054. The Greens were third in the poll, with their candidate Alan Johnson getting 517 votes Coun Davda said: “Over recent months, it has become increasingly clear to me that real, positive change for our neighbourhoods requires a fresh approach and a political home that puts fairness, community action, and the local environment at the heart of everything “Joining the Green Party is not a decision taken lightly or out of frustration with others, but out of a genuine belief that it offers the most constructive and community-focused path forward “My focus on the ground will not change, I will continue to work tirelessly for our residents every single day, and I remain committed to working collaboratively with colleagues across all parties for the good of Bolton .”

evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans The authority blamed a 'coding error' for the blunder and has apologised Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17 Bolton council sent out lett
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans The authority blamed a 'coding error' for the blunder and has apologised Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17 Bolton council sent out lett
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans The authority blamed a 'coding error' for the blunder and has apologised Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17 Bolton council sent out letters to residents incorrectly telling them they could not object to controversial housing plans on green belt land. It has emerged the major procedural error occurred in the authority’s handling of a Rowland Homes appeal on a Bolton council planning ref The town hall said the issue was due to a ‘coding error’ in generating the letters and has issued an apology to all affected residents In March this year the council’s planning committee threw out the plans after hearing fears the development could have ‘merged Bolton and Bury ’ Concerns about local biodiversity, traffic issues, and ‘green belt’ vs ‘grey belt’ land were central to the refusal, with the council deciding that the benefits of 80 extra houses did not outweigh the potential negatives An appeal against that decision was lodged by Rowland Homes and the case is set to be heard by the Planning inspectorate in the coming months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Altrincham An end to Altrincham's 20-year development saga could be in sight Plans for the site have ranged from a hospital to a bowling alley Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:14, 13 Oct 2026 View Image Land off Oakfield Roa Trafford council is pushing forward with plans to develop an Altrincham site that has stalled since 2007 Two competing visions are set to be considered by the council’s cabinet next week for the 4.5-acre site off Oakfield Road, previously known as Altair. One would be a residential-led scheme A spokeswoman said more than 100 new homes could be built there, if that approach is taken forward. Plan two could see a retail-led approach taken, with this most likely to include a large food store or supermarket Council documents indicate a preference for the former approach to be taken forwards. If that is the case, some ground-floor retail uses could also be incorporated, they add The land, near Altrincham Interchange, currently comprises the Planet Ice ice rink and around 320 parking spaces. Trafford council said the parking is important for the neighbouring Move Altrincham leisure site

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher knowingly dragged him under car for more than a mile after hitting him as he cycled home, trial told Simon Richardson denies murdering Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walk The man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins knowingly dragged the popular educator under his car for more than a mile after hitting him as he cycled home, a trial has been told Simon Richardson hit Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham in April, a court heard. The 56-year-old head was making his way home to Northwich, Cheshire, after work when he was struck at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, a jury was told He was dragged under the wheels of the car for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm, a court was told Mr Richardson, 35, earlier failed to properly observe a junction, 'flying straight through the give way markers', before hitting Mr Mullins, the court heard The defendant didn't stop and 'put his foot down', prosecutors alleged as a murder trial began on Tuesday (October 13). Mr Mullins was trapped under the car, the court heard, while his damaged bike was left in the road

evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Builder says 'it's a trap' as one Oldham bus lane camera hits him with double fine - with 4,200 others affected The Oldham camera issued over 4,000 fines between September 2024 and August 2026 Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barne A builder fears an Oldham bu
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Builder says 'it's a trap' as one Oldham bus lane camera hits him with double fine - with 4,200 others affected The Oldham camera issued over 4,000 fines between September 2024 and August 2026 Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barne A builder fears an Oldham bus lane camera is becoming a ‘revenue trap’ after he discovered thousands have been fined Chris Bagnall, a builder from Stoke-on-Trent, was driving along Ashton Road on the way to work in Oldham when he was hit by two fines for going into the end of a bus lane . He said he ‘did not think anything of it’ until the fines came through He said he never made the mistake again but feels he has been unfairly caught out. The bus lane comes to an end just before a junction with Bellfield Avenue He later submitted a Freedom of Information request to Oldham council which showed the single camera issued 4,205 penalty charge notices and raked in £95,014 in revenue between September 2024 and August 2026. In May 2026 alone, the camera issued 290 fines generating £8,026 in 31 He said: “In both instances, I merely moved over a couple of metres before the bus lane officially ended to prepare for the merge into the general traffic lane. There was no bus present, no queue was jumped, and zero advantage was gained

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Bee Network passengers suffer 'grave injuries' in major incident as driver pleads guilty Some 15 people were injured and a major incident declared when the Bee Network bus smashed into the bridge in Salford, tearing off its roof Add to preferr A bus driver who ploughed into a bridge while on 'auto-pilot' momentarily forgot he was behind the wheel of a double-decker, a court heard Some 15 people were injured, three seriously, and a major incident declared when the Bee Network bus smashed into the bridge as it entered a tunnel under the Bridgewater Canal on Barton Lane in Eccles, tearing off its roof One victim suffered a fractured skull and other numerous serious injuries when he was 'ejected' from the top deck Manchester Crown Court heard driver Christopher Henry ignored several 'low bridge' warnings in the moments before the crash before taking a wrong turn in the 100 service, from the Trafford Centre to Manchester city centre Earlier in his shift he had been on a different route, the 52, a single decker bus which went along Barton Lane. At the time of the crash Henry - a bus driver of 15 years experience - 'must have thought he was driving the 52 bus instead'

title: Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78

evidence_packet.title: Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78
evidence_packet.lead: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources New
evidence_packet.summary: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources New
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources News Dianne Bourne Lifestyle Editor 00:20, 14 Oct 2026 Updated 06:27, 14 Oct 2026 It's about as fitting as it gets that the final social media post from Councillor Pat Karney was one celebrating Manchester and Christmas , two of his greatest passions. No Relentlessly enthusiastic, and fiercely proud of his home city, he was always trying to make things better for the communities he served so tirelessly for the past 50 years As Manchester's self-appointed Christmas spokesperson, he was the man the council relied on to pull on an elf hat, the Christmas jumper, and ensure everyone was ready to celebrate - even if it was the start of November. He ensured the markets every year would get bigger and bette He was also instrumental in bringing the now annual Christmas Parade to life, after the success of the Manchester Day parade, his brainchild, was started in 2010. These events, which bring joy to thousands of people each year, are a special part of Pat's legacy But then Pat sure did love a parade - a regular at Manchester Pride, The St Patrick's Day Parade and Manchester Day. When his home patch of Harpurhey started its own parade in 2025, he hailed walking in it as "the proudest moment of my life."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Metrolink Hope for Metrolink commuters as bosses reveal 2027 tram closure plans The comments come as passengers brace for two more weeks of travel chaos from Monday Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:10, 14 Oct 2026 View 2 Ima Just one round of major tram works are on the cards for next year, transport bosses have promised. It comes as commuters brace themselves for two more weeks of travel chaos. Three major lines will be shut from Monday (October 19) until next month The closures are the second phase of works to ‘future proof’ the tracks around Cornbrook, Deansgate-Castlefield and Trafford Bar. Around four kilometres of rail which is coming to the end of its 30-year lifespan will be replaced, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has said The works, expected to finish by Sunday, November 1, will mean that no trams will run on the Altrincham , Eccles and Trafford Centre lines. Further disruptions will impact the East Didsbury and Manchester Airport lines, which will stop at Firswood, while the Rochdale line will st The network has been hit by a series of major works over the course of 2026, including a three-week closure on the same stretch during the summer But passengers will get a reprieve in 2027, with just one major round of work scheduled for the year, Metrolink network director Ian Davies said. That will again see the stations around Cornbrook close and is expected to take place over the Easter school holidays

title: Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule'

evidence_packet.title: Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule'
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester Airport Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule' He has hit out at the autopay system at Manchester Airport, but they have defended the fine Add to preferred s A man has slammed Manchester
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Airport Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule' He has hit out at the autopay system at Manchester Airport, but they have defended the fine Add to preferred s A man has slammed Manchester
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule' He has hit out at the autopay system at Manchester Airport, but they have defended the fine Add to preferred s A man has slammed Manchester Airport after his wife was issued a £100 fine - despite their car being registered for automatic payments at drop-off zones. Michael Joseph said the fine 'undermines the autopay system' after they were charged for dropping their son off at the airport The 52-year-old said his partner took their son to the Terminal 2 pick-up zone on September 23. The family, from Salford , previously set up autopay after having 'a bad experience with parking at the airport' The system allows people to register their vehicle online with a payment card and be automatically charged for pick-ups or drop-offs at the airport If drivers don't have autopay set up, they have to visit Manchester Airport's website - or call up - to pay charges by midnight the day after visits. Missing the payment deadline results in a £100 Parking Charge Notice View 4 Images They received the fine despite having an AutoPay account (Image: Manchester Evening News)

title: How '4,000 holes in Blackburn, Lancashire' are protecting us against wildfires

evidence_packet.title: How '4,000 holes in Blackburn, Lancashire' are protecting us against wildfires
evidence_packet.lead: Winter Hill fires How '4,000 holes in Blackburn, Lancashire' are protecting us against wildfires Eight years on from the devastating fires of 2018 Winter Hill is still recovering, but a huge new scheme to 'rewet' the moor hopes to prevent future disas Add to preferred sources Com
evidence_packet.summary: Winter Hill fires How '4,000 holes in Blackburn, Lancashire' are protecting us against wildfires Eight years on from the devastating fires of 2018 Winter Hill is still recovering, but a huge new scheme to 'rewet' the moor hopes to prevent future disas Add to preferred sources Com
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Winter Hill fires How '4,000 holes in Blackburn, Lancashire' are protecting us against wildfires Eight years on from the devastating fires of 2018 Winter Hill is still recovering, but a huge new scheme to 'rewet' the moor hopes to prevent future disas Add to preferred sources Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 05:48, 14 Oct 2026 The rain is coming down sideways. From just a few hundred yards away the 1,000ft high TV mast is invisible in the mist Underfoot the ground is so boggy it wobbles like blancmange. Stood halfway up Winter Hill on a sodden Monday morning, it's hard to imagine this was the scene of one of the UK's worst wild fires. But back in the summer of 2018 that's exactly what it was Then conditions on the moor on the border of Bolton and Blackburn were very different. The UK was in the midst of a prolonged heatwave leaving the grass and peat parched So, when a fire was started deliberately near the mast authorities were on high alert. To make matters worse the following day a second blaze broke out on another part of the moor And when on the third day the wind changed direction and the fires joined up, it was a recipe for disaster. At the height of the blaze 150 firefighters were battling the flames as helicopters dropped hundreds of thousands of litres of water on the moors

title: Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled

evidence_packet.title: Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled
evidence_packet.lead: Heaton Park Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C.
evidence_packet.summary: Heaton Park Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled Statements have been issued Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 18:20, 13 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Fontaines D.C
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Heaton Park Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled Statements have been issued Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 18:20, 13 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Fontaines D.C. (Image: Kenny Brown) A Jewish council has called for gigs at Heaton Park by Irish rock band Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled. The Jewish Representative Council of Greater Manchester and Region, in a statement on Tuesday, said it had 'concerns' over 'the potential consequences of inflammatory rhetoric f The Heaton Park shows - on July 3 and 4 next year - were announced last month. Fontaines D.C. also announced shows in Cardiff, Newcastle, Glasgow and London as part of a UK headline tour, and are set to be supported by Little Simz and Viagra Boys The band has expressed its support for Palestine at previous shows. Pictures show the phrases 'free Palestine' and 'Israel is committing genocide' appearing on screens during a gig by the band in London last year The JRC said it had 'registered [its] profound concerns' with Manchester council over the Heaton Park shows. The statement said it expected 'robust and adequate safeguards' to be in place 'to protect the Jewish community' In response, the council said addressing any concerns from the Jewish community would be 'front and centre in preparations for these events'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Gunman shot at woman before barricading himself in stranger's house in four-hour stand-off with armed police Adam Wass has been jailed Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 18:05, 13 Oct 2026 View 4 Images Adam Wass, 3 A gunman who shot at a woman before a four-hour standoff with armed police has been jailed. 'Dangerous' Adam Wass barricaded himself in a terrified stranger's house after twice pulling the trigger of a firearm in Salford He has now been locked up for six years. The 36-year-old, Greater Manchester Police said, put two innocent people through 'terrifying ordeals' Wass attempted to shoot at a woman on St Joseph's Drive, Ordsall, on February 1 this year. The weapon misfired and no bullet emerged from the chamber Wass pulled the trigger again as the woman ran and took cover behind a car. That time, a bullet was fired. GMP said Wass then went into a nearby home and threatened a man inside, who fled unhurt Armed officers were scrambled at around 8.15pm. Wass, who still had the gun, barricaded himself inside and refused to give himself up

title: Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans

evidence_packet.title: Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans The authority blamed a 'coding error' for the blunder and has apologised Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17 Bolton council sent out lett
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans The authority blamed a 'coding error' for the blunder and has apologised Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17 Bolton council sent out lett
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans The authority blamed a 'coding error' for the blunder and has apologised Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17 Bolton council sent out letters to residents incorrectly telling them they could not object to controversial housing plans on green belt land. It has emerged the major procedural error occurred in the authority’s handling of a Rowland Homes appeal on a Bolton council planning ref The town hall said the issue was due to a ‘coding error’ in generating the letters and has issued an apology to all affected residents In March this year the council’s planning committee threw out the plans after hearing fears the development could have ‘merged Bolton and Bury ’ Concerns about local biodiversity, traffic issues, and ‘green belt’ vs ‘grey belt’ land were central to the refusal, with the council deciding that the benefits of 80 extra houses did not outweigh the potential negatives An appeal against that decision was lodged by Rowland Homes and the case is set to be heard by the Planning inspectorate in the coming months

One would be a residential-led scheme A spokeswoman said more than 100 new homes could be built there, if that approach is taken forward. If that is the case, some ground-floor retail uses could also be incorporated, they add The land, near Altrincham Interchange, currently comprises the Planet Ice ice rink and around 320 parking spaces. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton councillor switches allegiance just 10 weeks after being elected New Green councillor Yusuf Davda said his decision had not been 'taken lightly or out of frustration with others' Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local dem A Bolton councillor who was elected 10 weeks ago has switched allegiance and joined the Green Party. Coun Yusuf Davda recently topped the poll in a by-election for Rumworth ward on July 30 as an Independent He gained 1.458 votes with Labour in second on 1,054. The Greens were third in the poll, with their candidate Alan Johnson getting 517 votes Coun Davda said: “Over recent months, it has become increasingly clear to me that real, positive change for our neighbourhoods requires a fresh approach and a political home that puts fairness, community action, and the local environment at the heart of everything “Joining the Green Party is not a decision taken lightly or out of frustration with others, but out of a genuine belief that it offers the most constructive and community-focused path forward “My focus on the ground will not change, I will continue to work tirelessly for our residents every single day, and I remain committed to working collaboratively with colleagues across all parties for the good of Bolton .”

The 56-year-old head was making his way home to Northwich, Cheshire, after work when he was struck at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, a jury was told He was dragged under the wheels of the car for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm, a court was told Mr Richardson, 35, earlier failed to properly observe a junction, 'flying straight through the give way markers', before hitting Mr Mullins, the court heard The defendant didn't stop and 'put his foot down', prosecutors alleged as a murder trial began on Tuesday (October 13). Mr Mullins was trapped under the car, the court heard, while his damaged bike was left in the road

evidence_packet.evidence_text: How one city became the centre of a social media circus In the aftermath of heavy rain, on a quiet street in East Salford, a woman is hurrying towards a terraced house. A little boy grasps her hand, smiling, breaking into sporadic skips as he tries to keep pace. Shards of glass litter the road and numerous windows have been covered wi This unassuming pair live in one of the five houses targeted on this street last week in a supposed attack on Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs). But the woman – who is black, in her 30s, and declines to give her name for obvious reasons – tells me that her house is not an HMO This woman and her neighbours were not the first people to be caught up in what has been described on social media as a “protest” against these kinds of properties. Any house or flat that’s rented out by three or more tenants – at least two of whom are unrelated – and where they Last week’s attacks have divided Salford, prompting public outrage, as well as praise, across social media. Facebook, Instagram and TikTok have grown rife with videos titled things like “SALFORD ERUPTS”. Much of the social media coverage on self-styled citizen journalist channels One image in particular, the words “No HMOs” scrawled across a boarded-up window, has been shared widely across social and mainstream media alike. While this message – daubed in black paint – was unambiguous, it seems the facts behind it are considerably less so

evidence_packet.evidence_text: They said they were "deeply saddened" by the decision to adopt the motion Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Altrincham's Green councillors Dan Jerrome, Geraldine Coggins and Michael Welton Green councillors in Trafford have publicly distanced themselves from their national party's controversial new policy on Zionism, warning that it could negatively af In a strongly worded statement, seven Green councillors, including representatives of Altrincham, said they were "deeply saddened" by the decision to adopt the motion at the party's national conference on Sunday The motion, entitled Zionism is Racism , was passed by 1,022 votes to 813 at the Green Party conference in Brighton It formally establishes the Greens as an anti-Zionist party, defines Zionism as a form of racism and supports the creation of a single democratic Palestinian state across historic Palestine, with Jerusalem as its capital But Trafford's Green councillors have made clear they oppose aspects of the policy, particularly its position on Palestinian statehood and its definition of Zionism

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Inspectors highlighted a school where pupils feel “safe and happy” Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Altrincham College has been praised by Ofsted for its personal development programme and sixth form, with inspectors highlighting a school where pupils feel “safe and happy” The Green Lane secondary school received two “Strong standard” judgements following its inspection in May, for personal development and wellbeing and its post-16 provision Achievement, attendance and behaviour, curriculum and teaching, inclusion, and leadership and governance were all judged to meet the “Expected standard”. Safeguarding standards were also met Under Ofsted's current grading system, a Strong standard means leaders are working above the standard expected of them, while an Expected standard means the school is fulfilling the expected standard of education or care Inspectors described Altrincham College's careers programme as “impressive”, saying pupils were “very well prepared” for future education, employment or training. evidence_packet.lead: Simon Richardson, 35, denies the murder of 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was struck and killed as he cycled home from work on 20 April Prosecutors claim Richardson stopped along the way, tried to dislodge the injured but still living cyclist, before driving on with Mullins rem
evidence_packet.summary: Simon Richardson, 35, denies the murder of 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was struck and killed as he cycled home from work on 20 April Prosecutors claim Richardson stopped along the way, tried to dislodge the injured but still living cyclist, before driving on with Mullins rem
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Simon Richardson, 35, denies the murder of 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was struck and killed as he cycled home from work on 20 April Prosecutors claim Richardson stopped along the way, tried to dislodge the injured but still living cyclist, before driving on with Mullins remaining trapped under the wheels He also denies an alternative count of manslaughter and one of dangerous driving - relating to a police chase the following day - and is standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Philip Barnes KC, opening the case for the prosecution, told the jury that "plainly fit" Mullins was cycling from Stretford Grammar School to his home in Northwich - his usual 19-mile (30-km) commute - at 18:07 BST on Paddock Lane in Warburton, Trafford As the married father-of-two approached the junction with Dunham Road, a black Volvo XC90 drove straight through give-way signs and road markings and struck the left side of his bike Barnes said Richardson, of no fixed address, did not stop and instead fled the scene towards Cheshire hitting speeds above 60mph

The campaign highlights the wellbeing benefits of reading, and each year encourages people of all ages to spend 10 minutes reading on and around World Mental Health Day (10 October). to help improve their mental health.. . title: Motion tabled to celebrate centenary of women's voting equality

evidence_packet.title: Motion tabled to celebrate centenary of women's voting equality
evidence_packet.lead: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men
evidence_packet.summary: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men
evidence_packet.evidence_text: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men Although some women were granted the right to vote in 1918, it was not until 1928 that all women over the age of 21 were granted the vote regardless of their occupation, wealth or ownership of property To mark this hugely significant milestone a Council motion has been set out to recognise and celebrate this moment in history It is no secret that Manchester played a huge part in the Women’s Suffrage movement. The Pankhurst name is known across the globe and is a byword for resilience and a refusal to give in to apparent insurmountable odds In 2018 a statue of Emmeline Pankhurst was proudly installed in St Peter’s Square and has since become a rallying point for people across the city to have their voices heard, and acts as a powerful reminder that history was made by women who refused to give up But the Pankhursts were also joined by thousands of ordinary Mancunian women whose names have been lost to history, but whose legacy still lives on a century later

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cllr Thomas Robinson has been chosen as the new Deputy Leader of Manchester City Council He fills the role vacated by Cllr Garry Bridges when he was elected Leader earlier this month and will serve alongside the other Deputy Leader, Cllr Tracey Rawlins His portfolio responsibilities will include work and skills, crime and safety and emergency planning Cllr Robinson has served as Executive Member for Health and Social Care since 2022 overseeing the adult social care service which was recently rated ‘Good’ by the Care Quality Commission, and has represented Clayton and Openshaw as a councillor since 2021 Raised in Ardwick, he has deep roots in Manchester and his experience growing up in a council flat amid a supportive community has shaped his commitment to public service and building a city where everyone can thrive regardless of background “As a born and bred Mancunian, to become the Deputy Leader of our city is truly humbling. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former pub transformed into sheltered accommodation for those struggling with homelessness has been described as a 'blueprint' to be replicated across the country Earlier this year, the former Queens Arms in Newtown was unveiled as a refurbished 14-bed sheltered accommodation, complete with kitchen and washing facilities, to give people in crisis a safe place to stay and receive further support to get back on their feet With homelessness in the national spotlight following Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s pledge to end rough sleeping, it is venues like the Queens Arms and the work of organisations like The Brick and Wigan Council that are being assessed to achieve these aims Councillor Susan Gambles, portfolio holder for housing and welfare, and chair of the homelessness and rough sleeping strategic partnership board, said: “There are some fantastic local partners that work collectively to support people at risk of homelessness, and we are so pleased “What comes across very strongly at their Queens Arms hub is that people are thriving there; they are positive, moving forward, and believing in themselves, and I think that is down to the facilities, the camaraderie, and the staff who care very deeply “This is the template that we should be using across the country, so we will continue championing these services and requesting more funding to be able to do even more like this.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Dame Meera Syal joins us to share the hilarious and heartwarming true stories that have shaped her life and work as one of Britain’s most beloved comedy legends Growing up in the only Asian family in a West Midlands mining village, Meera Syal wanted to take the stage long before anyone was ready to listen As one of the creators of Goodness Gracious Me, she changed British comedy forever. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

The plans include new station buildings at both the town centre and Edgeley entrances, alongs The new footbridge would make the existing tunnel used to reach the platforms largely redundant, while improved accessibility and public realm works are also planned around the station. Land off Shaw Heath is also being safeguarded for a future Metrolink station, tying the propos The project forms part of a broader regeneration of Stockport, following the opening of the new Stockport Interchange and ongoing works around the town centre. The station sits at the heart of this expansion, with fast services reaching Manchester Piccadilly in under 10 minutes a The plans have been described as a “once in a generation” opportunity to reshape one of the North’s best-connected rail hubs, with the public now being invited to have their say on the proposals The consultation will run from 8 Oct to 17 Nov and invites residents, businesses, rail passengers and community groups to view the early proposals and have their say

It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.title: Amad brands Man United loss a 'disgrace' in six-word reaction after Lisandro Martinez fury
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester United's loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League has been branded a 'disgrace' by Amad after Lisandro Martinez also let rip following the game
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester United's loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League has been branded a 'disgrace' by Amad after Lisandro Martinez also let rip following the game
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Amad Diallo Amad brands Man United loss a 'disgrace' in six-word reaction after Lisandro Martinez fury Manchester United's loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League has been branded a 'disgrace' by Amad after Lisandro Martinez also let rip following the game Amad dubbed Manchester United 's loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League a "f***ing disgrace", adding "I have no words" as a poor run of form continued These comments make up the caption of a post on his Snapchat account, which is verified as a Snap Star, denoted by the star next to the name on their profile. Amad , 24, started the match in Madrid among the substitutes and was introduced midway through the second half to replace Less than 10 minutes later, United had Leny Yoro sent off. They were already 1-0 down at the time, and then Ademola Lookman doubled Atletico's advantage Lisandro Martinez vented his fury in a post-match interview . He said: "I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it's a reflection of how our club is at the moment, you know?" "We (had) a fantastic season last season, and now we expect more from the top, from above, you know, to bring more players to compete, because many, many teams bring many players in as well, and today also, Atletico have an amazing team, and they deserved to win today."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
